# How the 🎈 Balloon Port was built: standards in, a unit out (run by a unit lead)

*7th grade math, Unit 2 (Georgia GADOE 7.NR.1.6 to 7.NR.1.9). Made by `scripts/builder/make-report.mjs` from `docs/builder/G7-UNIT2-LOG.md` on 2026-11-01 16:37 UTC. Rerun it whenever the log grows; do not edit this file by hand.*

## In one paragraph

The owner asked for Unit 2 "with less help" from the coordinating session, so it started the log and handed the whole run to a 🧭 unit lead. In 1 h 17 min of clock time (15:20 to 16:37 UTC), the unit lead wrote the spec and built the 4-station 🎈 Balloon Port with 8 skills at three levels, picked 11 videos, made 4 interactive note sheets and a game, Canyon Balloon Rally. Its session had no Agent tool, so it did those making roles itself, one after another (mapper, builder, videographer, worksheet maker, game designer); that work has no token count. For every check it started a fresh cloud session instead, so the builder still never checked its own work: an independent solver checked 9,600 Balloon Port problems on every step, and a blind solver took 288 unit-test items without the key (288 agreed). The checkers reported 5 things to fix and 24 judgment calls; each went back to the builder and was checked again. The owner's new rule, never two of the same choice, was checked 4 ways: the game's own self-test (36,000 hands, 0 repeats); the solver's every-step checker (STEP_ORACLES), which fails a repeated choice; the blind solver's scan of 6,000 more problems (0 repeats); and the looks review. The checkers' usage is exact: 36.18 million tokens, $16.86 at API prices as reported. The unit lead's own work isn't measured; at the checkers' cost per minute it would be about $1.51 more (a guess). A person still has to approve the note sheets, click each video once, play the shop on a phone and merge.

## What went wrong and was redone

- **The unit lead couldn't start agents.** Its session had no Agent tool, so it did 5 making roles itself, one after another (🗺️ mapper 4 min, 🏗️ builder 36 min, 🎬 videographer 2 min, 📝 worksheet maker 6 min, 🎮 game designer 7 min), and none of that work has a token count. It kept the checkers fresh by starting each as its own cloud session that may only add its own files.
- **Checker reports went to the wrong session.** A cloud session reports to the session that is its parent, which was the coordinating session, not the unit lead. The coordinating session relayed 4 reports; after that the unit lead read each session's result itself.
- **An answer key was rounded.** Some decimal answers had 4 places, but the key showed 3, so typing the answer she was shown was marked wrong (35 steps in 9,600 problems). The solver found it; the builder fixed it in round 2 (no divisor 16, and a guard); the solver confirmed it.
- **"What it means" choices took two more rounds.** After the round-2 fixes, the solver still found that the right size was always the smaller or the larger one, and some choices were still two-way. Round 3 picks the wrong size above or below at random; the solver's round 3 found them balanced.
- **Every story answer was negative.** Each problem passed every check on its own, but across many problems a student who always typed a negative never had to decide a sign. The blind solver saw it by looking at the spread; round 4 added rising, pay-back and warmer stories, and the solver confirmed about half positive.
- **Two more equal-value choice sets, one of them from Unit 1.** The looks review scanned 4,500 problems a skill by value and found two wrong options with the same value in a fraction step here (already fixed in round 4) and in the Dive Shop's subRat (Unit 1, live since Unit 1): a student can rule out both. The solver's repeated-choice check compares values only for plain numbers, so expressions like 2.9 + (−7.7) and 2.9 − 7.7 got past it. Fixed in builder round 5. It also found the help bot sending "multiplying negative numbers" to the 4th grade Toy Shop (fixed, with 3 new help-bot checks).
- **Two equal choices slipped into a practice step** ("Which fraction equals −(3/4)?"), the owner's "terrible mistake" again. The builder found it while moving that step onto tests and fixed it; the checkers' reports hadn't mentioned it, so it is worth asking the solver why its repeated-choice check didn't flag it.
- **The blind solve ran on older code.** It solved builder round 2 while round 3 was being made, so some of its findings were already fixed. No harm, but the report counts them once each.
- **The game crashed after the last gate,** and a label overlapped. The play-test at phone and desktop size found both; fixed before hand-off.
- **Videos still couldn't be opened.** YouTube is still blocked from the build computer, so ids come from search results only; 4 channels were inferred, not seen.

## What to change for Unit 3

- **Give the unit lead an Agent tool, or measure it.** Its making work is the biggest number this report can only guess. If it must work alone again, have it read its own usage at the start and end of each role.
- **Have the checker sessions report to the unit lead from the start** (it reads each result with `list_events`), so the coordinating session doesn't have to relay.
- **Add a check across many problems** (the sign of the answer about half each way, the right choice spread across positions and sizes) to `check-math`. Every per-problem check passed the all-negative stories; only the blind solver's spread caught them.
- **Make the repeated-choice checks read practice-only steps too**, so a repeat like the −(3/4) step is caught by a script, not by luck.
- **Put a ± on the fraction boxes** (on the feature list), so a fraction answer doesn't end with a separate sign choice.
- **Keep the exact usage.** The checkers' exact rows made their cost one number; with every role reporting the same way, the whole run would be.
- **Let the videographer reach YouTube** (or have a person check ids during the run) so ids are confirmed, not inferred.

## Cost: how it was worked out

Prices (Anthropic, per million tokens): input $4, output $20, cache read $0.20, cache write about $5.

*Andy runs this on a Claude plan, so this is usage against the plan, not a bill; the dollar figures are what the same work would cost at API prices. The real numbers are on the usage page.*

**Exact rows.** The four checker sessions (🧮 solver, 🙈 blind solver, 👀 fresh eyes, 🧾 reporter) ran as fresh cloud sessions; each reported its usage split into cache read, cache write, input and output, with the dollars. A running "total reported" replaces the earlier dollars, so each agent's last one is used. No estimate is needed for these rows.

| Agent | Cache read | Cache write | Input | Output | Total tokens | Reported cost | At the prices above |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 👀 Fresh eyes | 15,670,460 | 181,854 | 198 | 55,907 | 15,908,419 | $5.71 | $5.16 |
| 🧮 Solver | 11,908,297 | 200,222 | 1,136 | 67,037 | 12,176,692 | $5.33 | $4.73 |
| 🧾 Reporter | 4,079,780 | 172,576 | 49 | 66,743 | 4,319,148 | $3.53 | $3.01 |
| 🙈 Blind solver | 3,627,993 | 118,979 | 58 | 30,764 | 3,777,794 | $2.29 | $1.94 |
| **Total** | 35,286,530 | 673,631 | 1,441 | 220,451 | **36,182,053** | **$16.86** | $14.84 |

98% of these tokens are cache reads (the agent re-reading its own context each step), the cheapest kind. The "at the prices above" column uses our price table; the sessions' own figure is higher (they use their own rates), and the reported dollars are the ones used.

**The token counts in the log for the estimated rows are what the harness reported for each agent, not the billed total.** They very likely understate it: every tool call re-sends the agent's growing context (mostly as cache reads), so an agent with 221 tool calls reads far more than its reported count.

**Billed estimate.** Each tool call re-sends the agent's context. We assume the average context per call is half of that run's reported tokens, capped at 150k (high case: all of it, same cap), and price those re-reads as cache reads at $0.20 per million. The reported tokens themselves are priced as input and output (95% at $4, 5% at $20).

| Case | How | Billed tokens | Cost at API prices |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low | Only the reported tokens, priced at the "likely" mix below (no re-reads counted) | 612k | $1.26 |
| **Likely** | Re-reads: tool calls × half the run's reported tokens (at most 150k a call), as cache reads; reported tokens as input/output | about 33.76 million | **$9.57** |
| High | Same, with the full reported tokens per call (same cap) | about 33.76 million | $9.57 |

The reported counts have no input / output / cache split. Priced on their own (no re-reads), they come to:

| Mix | Assumed | $ per million tokens | Reported tokens only |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low (mostly cache reads) | 85% cache reads at $0.20, 10% fresh input at $4, 5% output at $20. Agents re-read the same files and chat history many times, and repeated reads are cached. | $1.57 | $0.96 |
| Likely (some caching) | 75% cache reads at $0.20, 10% cache writes at $5, 10% fresh input at $4, 5% output at $20. Our best guess for long agent runs. | $2.05 | $1.26 |
| High (no caching at all) | 95% input at $4 and 5% output at $20, as if nothing were cached. A ceiling, not a real case. | $4.80 | $2.94 |

**The unit lead** and **the lead** (the coordinating session) have no token count: their rows say "—". Same method as Unit 1's lead (a guess, kept out of the totals): the measured agents' cost per minute ($0.13 a minute at API prices) times the unmeasured minutes. For 12 min (Lead 12 min, about $1.51) that is about **$1.51** ($0.74 to $4.00, using the cheapest and the dearest measured agent per minute). With it, the run would come to about $27.94 at API prices. This is probably low for the unit lead: one long session that wrote the whole shop carries a much bigger context on every step than a short checker session, so its cost per minute is likely higher.

**A rough comparison with a person (an assumption, not a measurement).** Our guess for one experienced teacher who can also code, working alone, sized from the pieces the same way as Unit 1 (8 problem makers with pictures, 4 note sheets, one game). There is no timing data from a person doing this; treat it as a rough yardstick only. At $50 an hour:

| Task | Hours (assumed) |
|---|---|
| Write the Unit 2 spec (4 stations, 8 skills, levels, mix-ups) | 2 |
| Build the shop: 4 stations, 8 skills, rewards, wiring, room | 6 |
| 8 problem generators at 3 levels, with the balloon pictures | 18 |
| 4 interactive note sheets with checked, hidden answers | 16 |
| Find and vet 11 videos for 4 stations | 4 |
| A game for the unit, with a script that checks every hand | 8 |
| Independent answer check, a blind test solve, fixes, testing | 10 |
| **Total** | **64 hours, about $3,200** |

Against that: about 1 h 17 min of clock time and $26.43 measured (plus about $1.51 unmeasured, a guess) at API prices, plus the owner's time to review. The agents' work still needs that review; the person's would too.

## Unit 1 vs Unit 2

Both columns come from the same code run on each unit's log (`docs/builder/G7-UNIT1-LOG.md` and `docs/builder/G7-UNIT2-LOG.md`).

| | Unit 1 | Unit 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Clock time | 1 h 38 min | 1 h 17 min |
| Agent time (all rows added up) | 3 h 35 min | 3 h 42 min |
| Tokens | 1.91 million reported; about 60.14 million billed (estimate) | 36.18 million exact (Fresh eyes, Solver, Reporter, Blind solver) + 612k reported, about 33.76 million billed (est.) |
| Cost at API prices (measured) | about $20.83 (estimate, $3.92 to $25.50) | $26.43 (exact part reported, rest estimated) |
| Not measured | Lead and Feature keeper, 1 h 1 min: a guess of about $8.27 more | Lead, 12 min: a guess of about $1.51 more |
| Findings the checkers reported | 2 FIX, 9 judgment calls; also a picture that gave the answer away, a crash, a question with two right answers, 8 small looks fixes | 5 FIX, 24 judgment calls; also 2 bugs the builder caught in its own review, a crash and a label overlap in the game play-test, two equal choices in one practice step (found while fixing) |
| Builder rounds | 5 | 5 |
| The coordinating session stepping in | None: the lead did the coordination itself (11 lead rows) | Passed on 2 owner notes and relayed 4 checker reports |

- **Not like for like.** Unit 2's measured numbers are only the checker sessions (Fresh eyes, Solver, Reporter, Blind solver); the unit lead's making work isn't measured. In Unit 1 the measured agents covered all the making, and only the lead and feature keeper (1 h 1 min) were left out. So Unit 2's measured cost is lower mostly because less of it was measured.
- **Exact vs estimate.** Unit 1's tokens are estimates from one reported count per agent (re-reads at half that count a call, at most 150k). Unit 2's checker rows are exact: on their first runs they used about solver 157k, blind solver 135k tokens per tool call, nearly all cache reads. That is about the most Unit 1's estimate allows per call, a hint (from different agents, so not proof) that Unit 1's estimate is more likely low than high.
- **Stepping in.** In Unit 1 the lead was the coordinating session and did the coordination itself. In Unit 2 the coordinating session handed the run over and still stepped in: it passed on 2 owner notes and relayed 4 checker reports.
